text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000268 bills 99215 well above complexity-adjusted expectation in every complexity band, but documentation is too thin to confirm or refute upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess 99215 use is not explained by panel acuity. The provider's 99215 share runs roughly two to three times the all-provider share in every complexity band, including patients with zero or one chronic condition. The low-complexity sample includes visits with simple, acute-appearing diagnoses such as J06.9 (C0140784, C0141230, C0141104), Z09 (C0140169) and N39.0 (C0140997), which is the pattern most consistent with upcoding. Against that, the high-complexity sample (e.g., C0140829, C0140930) looks appropriate for 99215, and all three documented 99215 claims (C0140304, C0140536, C0140798) supported high MDM. Records came back for only about 1% of claims, so the documentation neither clears nor implicates the provider. The one cloned-data signal (one of nine moderate-plus data-reviewed notes with no lab line) is weak. A reviewer should first request charts specifically for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, starting with the acute-diagnosis visits, to see whether the notes support high MDM or 40+ minutes."}
